title: A Weekly Wrap: Market Movements, Trade News, and Earnings Highlights
summary: Eisman continues to separate market expectations from company results. He discusses a preliminary UK trade framework, private-equity liquidity, possible AI disruption of search, Netflix leadership and uneven corporate earnings. Two semiconductor explanations need correction: Marvell kept its guidance midpoint unchanged, and Arm earns licensing and royalty revenue rather than manufacturing chips.
assessment: The strongest lesson is to inspect details behind headlines and company excuses. The Marvell interpretation fails that standard in this episode. Streaming leadership is an operating assessment, not proof of a completed permanent contest or a stock recommendation.
framework_points: Read the actual terms of policy and guidance changes.
Distinguish an economic slowdown from company-specific weakness.
Look at distributions and realizations rather than private-market marks alone.
Separate an industry winner from a permanently closed competitive market.
Assess the expectations already reflected in price.
transcript_cautions: Auto-captions garble Marvell, Molson Coors and several EPS figures.
The 100% foreign-film tariff is discussed as a vague proposal, not an implemented tax.
Reported Apple testimony is not independently transcribed or authenticated in this review.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: The proposed foreign-film tariff and AI-export-rule changes are too vague to value confidently from the announcement alone.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Identify enacted text, coverage, effective dates and replacement rules.
claims.reason: He asks for missing implementation details and does not provide a specific price forecast.
claims.next_check: Identify enacted text, coverage, effective dates and replacement rules.

claims.claim: The UK announcement is a preliminary framework, not yet a comprehensive trade agreement.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Read operative commitments and distinguish them from negotiating intentions.
claims.reason: The official document sets out general terms and further negotiations.

evidence.title: US-UK economic prosperity deal general terms
evidence.finding: The document sets out general terms and future negotiations, including sector-specific treatment. It was a framework rather than a completed comprehensive free-trade agreement.

claims.next_check: Read operative commitments and distinguish them from negotiating intentions.

claims.claim: A possible implication of the UK deal is a 10% minimum tariff for every trading partner.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define countries, products, exemptions and the period over which a floor is expected.
claims.reason: This is presented as a possible policy inference. Sectoral exceptions and changing arrangements prevent treating it as a universal realized rule.
claims.next_check: Define countries, products, exemptions and the period over which a floor is expected.

claims.claim: Carried interest can receive capital-gains treatment despite rewarding management services, which he regards as unfair.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate the normative proposal from the actual statutory tax treatment.
claims.reason: The fairness judgment is normative. The description is simplified and does not specify the holding-period and interest-type rules needed for a complete tax analysis.
claims.next_check: Separate the normative proposal from the actual statutory tax treatment.

claims.claim: Weak exits reduce cash returned to private-equity investors and create pressure for liquidity.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track realizations, distributions, financing and unfunded commitments.
claims.reason: The mechanism follows from the fund cash-flow structure: fewer realized proceeds constrain distributions unless another funding source is used. It does not establish the size of the aggregate exit drought.
claims.next_check: Track realizations, distributions, financing and unfunded commitments.

assumptions: A closed-end fund primarily distributes realized investment proceeds and does not fully replace missing proceeds with borrowing.
proof.derivation: Lower exit cash proceeds reduce cash available for distributions, even if reported asset values remain unchanged.

claims.claim: University endowments considering secondary sales may reveal discounts to private-equity carrying values.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare completed transaction proceeds, reference NAV dates and excluded assets.
claims.reason: The episode reports prospective transactions, not completed audited sale prices.
claims.next_check: Compare completed transaction proceeds, reference NAV dates and excluded assets.

claims.claim: Reported first-time Safari search declines are an early warning that AI may weaken Google search economics.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Check original testimony, total queries, browser mix and search monetization.
claims.reason: The reported channel data are relevant if authenticated, but one browser-month does not establish total query decline, attribution to AI or revenue impairment.
claims.next_check: Check original testimony, total queries, browser mix and search monetization.

claims.claim: Mixed earnings can produce a rally when investors had already priced a much worse outcome.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare pre-release expected cash flows with the new information.
claims.reason: This is a conditional valuation mechanism, not proof of why this particular rally occurred.
claims.next_check: Compare pre-release expected cash flows with the new information.

assumptions: Price reflects expected future cash flows discounted for risk.
proof.derivation: Information can raise expected value relative to a pessimistic prior even when the reported level of activity is weak.

claims.claim: Guidance reductions at autos and household staples reinforce evidence of consumer caution.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate volume, price, input-cost and inventory effects.
claims.reason: Tariff costs and company-specific factors also affect guidance, so profit revisions are not a pure demand measure. The broader mixed-consumer assessment has support.

evidence.title: GM revised 2025 guidance
evidence.finding: GM issued lower guidance on May 1 including an estimated $4-5 billion tariff impact. Thus the earlier suspension was followed by a new forecast before this wrap.

evidence.title: McDonald Q1 2025 results
evidence.finding: US comparable sales declined 3.6%, supporting a weaker consumer-facing operating example.

claims.next_check: Separate volume, price, input-cost and inventory effects.

claims.claim: Molson Coors decline is too large to attribute simply to macro uncertainty.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile brand volume, shipment volume, inventory movements and discontinued business.
claims.reason: The issuer itself identifies contract-brewing exits and inventory comparisons alongside category weakness, supporting the need for a company-specific explanation.

evidence.title: Molson Coors Q1 2025 results
evidence.finding: Sales declined 11.3%; the issuer identified category weakness, prior-year inventory effects, lost contract brewing volume and other company-specific comparisons.

claims.next_check: Reconcile brand volume, shipment volume, inventory movements and discontinued business.

claims.claim: Travel and consumer results remain mixed, with Expedia weaker but Uber and Lyft showing booking strength.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare like-for-like bookings and margins, distinguishing market share from aggregate demand.
claims.reason: The comparative thesis requires consistent gross-booking, currency and geographic measures. Those detailed releases are not attached here.
claims.next_check: Compare like-for-like bookings and margins, distinguishing market share from aggregate demand.

claims.claim: Disney results and raised guidance show improving operating momentum.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Check segment performance and the revised earnings assumptions.
claims.reason: The issuer reports higher adjusted earnings and a stronger outlook, including better streaming economics.

evidence.title: Disney fiscal Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Disney reported higher adjusted EPS, raised its annual adjusted EPS growth outlook and improved streaming profitability.

claims.next_check: Check segment performance and the revised earnings assumptions.

claims.claim: Netflix has become the leading streaming business while legacy media lost ground by failing to adapt.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare subscribers, engagement, margins and cash returns while separating structural and managerial effects.
claims.reason: Netflix profitability supports its competitive strength. A claim that the contest is permanently won, or that management failure alone explains all legacy value loss, is broader than the evidence.

evidence.title: Netflix Q1 2025 shareholder letter
evidence.finding: Netflix reported strong revenue and operating profitability. This supports business strength, not a literal final end to streaming competition.

evidence.title: Disney fiscal Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Disney reported higher adjusted EPS, raised its annual adjusted EPS growth outlook and improved streaming profitability.

claims.next_check: Compare subscribers, engagement, margins and cash returns while separating structural and managerial effects.

claims.claim: Disney should remain a viable streaming competitor, while other survivors are uncertain.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define sustained streaming profitability, market share and a time horizon.
claims.reason: No success threshold or forecast horizon is specified; it is a qualified competitive judgment.
claims.next_check: Define sustained streaming profitability, market share and a time horizon.

claims.claim: Rockwell would benefit from reshoring, but cost-cut-driven improvement should not be read as broad economic strength.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate organic orders, cost savings and attributable reshoring projects.
claims.reason: The distinction between cost reduction and demand is useful, while the size of the reshoring benefit and company-specific attribution require orders and margin evidence.
claims.next_check: Separate organic orders, cost savings and attributable reshoring projects.

claims.claim: Johnson Controls and Emerson results are stable rather than evidence of an industrial boom.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare organic sales, orders and earnings excluding restructuring and acquisition effects.
claims.reason: This comparative operating assessment is not independently resolved from the company-specific primary data attached in this review.
claims.next_check: Compare organic sales, orders and earnings excluding restructuring and acquisition effects.

claims.claim: Marvell makes traditional chips rather than having a significant AI-infrastructure role.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect product and revenue exposure to custom accelerators and data-center networking.
claims.reason: The contemporaneous company release explicitly describes custom AI silicon and its expanding opportunity. Distinguishing Marvell from Nvidia does not make it a non-AI business.

evidence.title: Marvell guidance clarification and AI webinar
evidence.finding: The revenue midpoint remained $1.875 billion; the range narrowed from plus/minus 5% to plus/minus 2%. The same release emphasized custom AI silicon and postponed investor day.

claims.next_check: Inspect product and revenue exposure to custom accelerators and data-center networking.

claims.claim: Narrowing guidance means the company is taking guidance down.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the old and new midpoint separately from upper and lower bounds.
claims.reason: Marvell explicitly reaffirmed the midpoint while reducing the width of the range. Range precision and a lower central forecast are different changes.

evidence.title: Marvell guidance clarification and AI webinar
evidence.finding: The revenue midpoint remained $1.875 billion; the range narrowed from plus/minus 5% to plus/minus 2%. The same release emphasized custom AI silicon and postponed investor day.

claims.next_check: Compare the old and new midpoint separately from upper and lower bounds.

claims.claim: AMD export restrictions can offset otherwise strong quarterly operating performance.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate lost revenue, inventory charges and expected future demand.
claims.reason: The issuer disclosed material export-control-related charges and outlook effects. The exact claimed revenue loss and share-price causality are not resolved by the charge alone.

evidence.title: AMD Q1 2025 results
evidence.finding: Export restrictions affected the outlook and led to an estimated $800 million inventory-related charge, despite strong reported quarterly revenue.

claims.next_check: Separate lost revenue, inventory charges and expected future demand.

claims.claim: Arm designs and manufactures semiconductor technology.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Identify who owns fabrication and finished-chip inventory and how Arm earns revenue.
claims.reason: Arm designs and licenses IP, with royalties from customers chips. Treating it as a chip manufacturer misstates the economic model, though designs semiconductor technology is correct.

evidence.title: Arm fiscal Q4 2025 shareholder letter
evidence.finding: Arm reports licensing and royalty revenue from its intellectual-property model, not manufacturing semiconductor devices itself.

claims.next_check: Identify who owns fabrication and finished-chip inventory and how Arm earns revenue.

claims.claim: Arm cautious outlook is a sign of tariff uncertainty reaching semiconductors.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Read forecast assumptions and compare licensing timing with customer unit demand.
claims.reason: An issuer forecast can reflect customer timing, licensing concentration and tariffs; the episode does not isolate their effects.
claims.next_check: Read forecast assumptions and compare licensing timing with customer unit demand.
